invariant: Maximum 500 LOC per source file; decompose when nearing 450
rationale: Bounds per-file complexity and keeps files reviewable and agent-sized
sensor: bash scripts/check-loc.sh (loc sensor)

invariant: `unwrap()` and `expect()` are forbidden in all Rust sources
rationale: Typed, recoverable errors at boundaries; panics are never an acceptable failure mode
sensor: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings (unwrap_used/expect_used deny) + python3 scripts/validate-structure.py

invariant: No unsafe code in the workspace
rationale: Eliminates undefined-behavior classes from the privacy boundary
sensor: cargo check --workspace (workspace lint unsafe_code = forbid)

invariant: Runtime crates stay provider-agnostic: no cloud LLM SDK or network-client dependency
rationale: The privacy boundary must work offline and never leak context to a provider
sensor: bash scripts/check-deps.sh (layer direction + cargo deny check + the offline ban list: Cargo.lock must contain no network client, TLS stack, or hosted-model SDK, checked across every feature) + review of new dependency entries

invariant: Every detector, judge, policy, transformer, and vault implementation stays replaceable behind plugin-api traits
rationale: Capabilities must remain swappable and testable in isolation
sensor: cargo check --workspace (implementations compile against plugin-api) + cargo test -p do-context-shield-plugin-registry (known_names_construct, json_vault_is_registered_and_needs_its_path, regex_name_detects_and_hybrid_name_pairs_it_with_the_model) + review of new capability crates

invariant: Registry names map to the intended plugins and unknown names fail with a capability-naming error; `hybrid` wires regex together with the model half, so it fails closed without a model_dir instead of degrading to regex
rationale: The names are the user-facing selection surface for CLI and MCP; a silently remapped or degraded name would change what detects and transforms without any other sensor noticing
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-plugin-registry

invariant: Secrets are redacted, never pseudonymized; personal identifiers are pseudonymized
rationale: A reversible token for a secret would defeat the redaction guarantee
sensor: cargo test --workspace (privacy-core pipeline tests)

invariant: Raw sensitive input, vault mappings, and restored secrets are never logged or echoed outside the sanitized/blob contract
rationale: Logs and error messages are context that can leave the machine
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-core --test privacy_invariants && cargo test -p do-context-shield-mcp-server (raw-value egress assertions)

invariant: Stage error text is scrubbed of the values the pipeline has seen (input plus detected entity values) before it leaves, so a plugin that formats raw input or an original value into its error cannot leak it to stderr, an MCP response, or a log
rationale: Plugins are replaceable and their error strings are arbitrary; the pipeline, not the backend, owns the guarantee that raw values never cross the boundary
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-core (leaking_detector_error_is_scrubbed, leaking_judge_error_is_scrubbed, leaking_vault_error_is_scrubbed)

invariant: Mappings are scoped by an explicit session id; restore resolves only tokens of the same scope and vault
rationale: Prevents cross-task placeholder resolution and leaks between concurrent agents
sensor: cargo test --workspace (scope-isolation tests in privacy-core, plugin-process, mcp-server)

invariant: Built-in memory and JSON vault mappings embed 64 bits of OS entropy per mapping (`__DO_PRIVATE_<KIND>_<N>_<16 hex>__`); legacy JSON tokens are never accepted as live aliases and are rotated when their mapping is reused
rationale: `restore` substitutes any token that matches a stored mapping; with predictable tokens a hostile model could enumerate session values it was never shown, or trick a harness into restoring fabricated placeholders. Per-mapping entropy makes guessing infeasible while repeated entities keep one stable pseudonym through the vault lookup, and rotating legacy mappings prevents an upgrade from preserving the old oracle.
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-vault-memory -p do-context-shield-vault-json (fabricated_tokens_do_not_resolve, legacy_tokens_are_not_resolved_and_are_rotated_on_reinsert) + cargo test -p do-context-shield-plugin-api

invariant: Every JsonVault resolve reads a fresh shared-locked snapshot, so a long-lived process observes external inserts and deletions and cannot restore a forgotten mapping
rationale: A cached vault state can outlive a separate process's forget or file deletion and disclose a raw value after retention was supposedly revoked; disk state must remain authoritative for every restore lookup.
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-vault-json (an_existing_instance_observes_external_scope_deletion)

invariant: ProcessVault get_or_insert succeeds only after an exact vault_resolve round-trip, and built-in minting rejects entity kinds that cannot be represented as restorable tokens
rationale: A shape-valid child token that its own store cannot resolve would make sanitize report success while restoration is impossible; malformed kind delimiters would likewise create tokens the restore scanner cannot parse.
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-plugin-process (rejects_a_well_shaped_token_that_cannot_be_resolved, rejects_a_token_resolved_to_a_different_mapping) + cargo test -p do-context-shield-plugin-api (invalid_kinds_cannot_be_minted)

invariant: Process plugins fail closed: malformed response, invalid span, undecided entity, leftover value, unresolvable placeholder, a response past the 8 MiB cap, or non-zero exit stops the call instead of passing text through
rationale: A permissive plugin turns the privacy boundary into a passthrough
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-plugin-process

invariant: MCP stdio tools/list stays in fixed order with ttlMs/cacheScope metadata, the server/discover and initialize paths resolve to identical tool behavior, server/discover carries resultType, a request `_meta.protocolVersion` is read (a missing one only warns, never rejects), and tool executions report failures as `isError` results while protocol failures (malformed JSON-RPC, unknown method/tool, non-object arguments, disabled tool) stay JSON-RPC errors
rationale: Clients cache tool lists; order and metadata drift breaks that contract silently
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-mcp-server + cargo test -p do-context-shield (tests/mcp_stdio.rs: tool_failure_is_an_iserror_result, meta_version_warning_goes_to_stderr_for_legacy_requests)

invariant: GLiNER2 stays behind the opt-in gliner2 feature, requires a local model directory, and fails closed without one — including a single-file export whose `config.json` is missing or carries no usable `id2label` map, which would otherwise decode every token as `O` and report zero entities
rationale: Heavy ONNX dependencies must not burden the default build, models are never fetched automatically, and a misconfigured export must never look like a clean scan
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-detector-gliner2 --features gliner2 (feature tests: id2label fail-closed, layout rejection; the Linux CI job runs them via --all-features) + cargo check -p do-context-shield-detector-gliner2 --features gliner2 (feature build; not part of the default suite)

invariant: Conventional commits with a type prefix; PR titles stay conventional because squash merges reuse them as the commit subject
rationale: Machine-parseable history for release drafting and commitlint
sensor: bash scripts/check-commitlint.sh (commitlint sensor) + CI action-semantic-pull-request

invariant: Agent skills pass the structure gate and carry graded eval fixtures
rationale: Skills are load-bearing feedforward guides; unvalidated guidance drifts silently
sensor: bash scripts/check-skills.sh (skills sensor) + do-harness eval --strict-fixtures

invariant: A change is complete only when verification evidence for its signal set is green
rationale: Exit codes and recorded evidence, not self-assessment, prove completion
sensor: do-harness verify --set verification --record + do-harness status --set verification

invariant: A sensor failing 3 consecutive times on the same subtask halts the loop and records its error signature
rationale: Blind re-runs of a broken sensor waste the loop and hide the defect
sensor: do-harness verify --record (strike counters) + do-harness errors list

invariant: Hooks come from .githooks via core.hooksPath; do-harness hook install into .git/hooks is the per-developer alternative, never both at once
rationale: A core.hooksPath pointing at .githooks makes git ignore .git/hooks entirely
sensor: bash scripts/check-hooks.sh (hooks sensor: hook files executable, every sensor declared in do-harness.toml [hooks] really invoked by that hook, core.hooksPath pinned to .githooks, and no combined .git/hooks + core.hooksPath mode) + do-harness doctor (state-db skew only; for the pinned v0.1.1 it reports managed-hook presence for .git/hooks and cannot see the .githooks mode)

invariant: Semantic judges classify existing candidates only: they return labels and confidence, never spans or text, and a judge can never downgrade a secret-like kind from redaction
rationale: A judge that could invent spans or rewrite values would move the privacy boundary into a model
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-core -p do-context-shield-policy-default

invariant: A judge failure, an out-of-range or duplicated judgment index, or an out-of-range confidence fails the sanitize call closed
rationale: A judge trusted without validation turns a malformed response into a silent policy bypass
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-core -p do-context-shield-plugin-process

invariant: Recipient-aware default policy enforces GDPR/jurisdiction data categories: special-category data addressed to external or unknown recipients blocks, and unknown recipients block non-secret data except when it is explicitly declared non-personal
rationale: Fail-closed boundary prevents sensitive personal data from leaking to unvetted recipients
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-policy-default -p do-context-shield-core

invariant: Detector output is validated centrally for a non-empty kind, confidence in 0..=1, UTF-8 character boundaries, input bounds, value matching, and non-overlapping spans before judging or planning; overlaps resolve longest-span-wins via plugin-api::resolve_overlaps, so a later span displacing a shorter overlapping one is kept (a later span that covers less text never wins)
rationale: Downstream pipeline stages (judge, policy, transformer) must never encounter corrupted offsets or overlapping entity replacements, and a leftmost-first dedup would drop a longer later span (for example a credential starting inside a shorter entity), leaving the uncovered tail of the value raw in the sanitized output; an empty kind or NaN/out-of-range confidence from an in-process detector must fail the call closed instead of reaching policy decisions or results
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-core (tests::a_later_span_that_is_longer_displaces_a_shorter_overlapping_one, tests::overlapping_spans_resolved_to_longest)

invariant: Overlap resolution is one shared implementation: detectors, the process-plugin decoder, and the central pipeline validation call plugin-api::resolve_overlaps instead of hand-rolling a sort-and-retain pass, and the rule reads longest-span-wins with equal lengths keeping the reported order
rationale: Four copies of the sort-and-retain loop drifted into leftmost-first while the docs and plugin checklists promised longest-span-wins, so the same overlap shape resolved differently per detector and a dropped longer span left raw text in sanitized output
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-plugin-api (resolve_overlaps tests), cargo test -p do-context-shield-plugin-process (detector_protocol::a_later_longer_span_wins_over_the_leftmost_one), cargo test -p do-context-shield-detector-gliner2 (decode_keeps_the_longest_overlapping_span)

invariant: Vault lifecycle supports explicit session deletion and TTL expiration; JSON vault serializes concurrent writers via file locking
rationale: Session cleanup bounds storage and protects privacy after agent tasks conclude; file locking prevents race conditions in multi-process workflows
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-vault-memory -p do-context-shield-vault-json

invariant: JSON vault persistence surfaces every write failure before renaming, so a failed flush can never replace a healthy vault file or report success; a vault file deleted outside the process reloads as empty instead of resurrecting stale mappings
rationale: A BufWriter discards flush errors when it drops, which silently corrupted the vault on ENOSPC/I/O failure while the insert reported success; and honoring an external deletion is what keeps the on-disk file the source of truth for sequential processes
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-vault-json (write_state_surfaces_flush_failures, failed_write_keeps_the_existing_vault, externally_deleted_vault_starts_over)

invariant: MCP tools reside in the context.* namespace and context.restore strictly requires an explicit session
rationale: Restoration resolves raw values and must never default to a shared or implicit session scope
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-mcp-server

invariant: The MCP surface defaults to the model-safe tool set: `mcp-stdio` exposes only `context.sanitize` and `context.inspect` unless `--tools`, `DO_CONTEXT_SHIELD_TOOLS`, or `[plugins] tools` opts into `restore`/`forget`/`all` (CLI flag > environment > file > default), because MCP tool results return to the calling model and a model-driven restore hands raw values into the context the boundary protects
rationale: Restore resolves raw values and forget destroys mappings; exposing them to a prompt-injected model lets it un-sanitize text it holds or destroy the harness's ability to restore. The fail-closed default keeps the model-facing surface non-revealing, and the CLI remains the harness-side restore path.
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-mcp-server + cargo test -p do-context-shield (tests/mcp_stdio.rs, tests/cli_errors.rs)

invariant: Adapter context surfaces default to the most restrictive ProcessingContext and reject unknown recipient/data_category names or wrong argument types instead of silently downgrading
rationale: A typo in a client-supplied trust classification must fail the call, never weaken the recipient-aware policy
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-mcp-server + CLI value parsers (clap value_parser + sanitize smoke)

invariant: Adapter argument surfaces are enforced, not just declared: CLI sanitize/restore/forget require an explicit --session, and MCP tools/call rejects a non-object `arguments` or a missing/non-string `text` instead of silently operating on empty input
rationale: An implicit session scope lets concurrent tasks resolve each other's placeholders, and a silent empty-input success hides a malformed client call behind a plausible response
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield (tests/cli_errors.rs session_is_required_exits_2) + cargo test -p do-context-shield-mcp-server (errors::argument_validation_failures_are_iserror_results, errors::unknown_method_malformed_json_and_bad_params_are_protocol_errors)

invariant: Session mappings are deletable through explicit forget surfaces (MCP context.forget, CLI forget) that require a session, and a process vault must confirm deletion with deleted=true or the call fails closed
rationale: Retention must be bounded and a child that silently ignores a wipe would leave raw values resolvable
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-core -p do-context-shield-plugin-process -p do-context-shield-mcp-server

invariant: The configuration file may only select known plugins and context names; unknown fields or values fail startup, and precedence is CLI flag > DO_CONTEXT_SHIELD_* environment variable > file value > built-in default, with every source validated the same way
rationale: A config typo must never silently select a weaker plugin, and effective settings must not depend on which clap default happened to be compiled in or which source supplied a value
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield --bins (config module tests: unknown field/value rejected, CLI-over-config precedence, tools validation) + cargo test -p do-context-shield --test cli_config (env-over-file, flag-over-env, invalid env override, auto-discovery)

invariant: CLI and MCP stdio behavior is tested black-box against the compiled `do-context-shield` binary, spawned with a hermetic working directory and `$HOME` so ambient config files can never change a test outcome
rationale: Behavior in the shipped artifact, not library internals, is the contract; a test reading the developer's real HOME or cwd config would be non-reproducible
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield (tests/cli_*.rs and tests/mcp_stdio.rs)

invariant: Detector overlap dedup keeps the longest span (plugin-api::resolve_overlaps) and resolves equal-span ties by SPECS order: more specific kinds precede looser shapes, and semantic post-filters (Luhn for card numbers, ABA for US routing numbers, byte-bounded octets for IPv4, ISO 13616 mod-97 for IBAN) run before dedup
rationale: A looser pattern can match exactly the same text as a more specific kind, so list order decides the reported kind; filtering invalid candidates after dedup would silently drop the specific match, and a leftmost-first dedup would keep a shorter early span over a longer one that starts inside it
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-detector-regex (overlap cases + luhn_gate_rejects_invalid_card_numbers, aba_gate_rejects_invalid_routing_numbers)

invariant: CodeQL code scanning runs through GitHub default setup (rust, python, actions) and must stay configured, because the main branch ruleset requires code-scanning results before a pull request can merge
rationale: With default setup disabled, or with no analysis on the target branch, the ruleset's code_scanning rule can never be satisfied and every merge needs an administrator bypass; an advanced-setup workflow added alongside default setup fails at analysis upload instead of taking over
sensor: gh api repos/d-oit/do-context-shield/code-scanning/default-setup (state=configured) + gh api repos/d-oit/do-context-shield/rulesets/rule-suites (code_scanning rule result)

invariant: Hybrid detector merge keeps primary spans authoritative and resolves secondary-secondary overlaps longest-span-wins, keeping the earlier-returned span on equal lengths
rationale: The merged list must carry no overlapping secondary spans so hybrid output is stable before the pipeline's own dedup pass, while primary precedence stops a noisy model fragment from splitting an authoritative structured-identifier span
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-detector-hybrid

invariant: The GLiNER2 backend loads ONNX Runtime dynamically and needs a runtime matching the ort release it was built against (1.28.x for ort 2.0.0-rc.13, supplied via ORT_DYLIB_PATH or the loader path)
rationale: ort is built with load-dynamic, so a missing or mismatched runtime fails at engine load; the version pin plus the official archive command is what users need to bring the model backend up
sensor: docs/plugins.md runtime note (pinned 1.28.x / ort 2.0.0-rc.13, verified 2026-09-20 with the fp16_v2 export) + GitHub CI: the Linux `Test` job fetches the pinned 1.28.0 archive, caches it, exports ORT_DYLIB_PATH and sets DO_HARNESS_REQUIRE_ORT=1 (so the runtime-backed tests fail instead of skipping; missing ORT_DYLIB_PATH is a failure) + gated model-backed E2E (cargo test -p do-context-shield --features gliner2 --test cli_model_e2e, which stays manual: it also needs DO_CONTEXT_SHIELD_E2E_MODEL_DIR)

invariant: CI runs the workspace tests on Linux with --all-features and on macOS and Windows with default features plus `cargo check --workspace --all-features --all-targets`, so platform-specific breakage in both default and feature-gated code is caught before merge
rationale: The CLI and MCP server ship as cross-platform binaries; Linux-only CI silently missed a Windows TOML path-escaping defect the first matrix run surfaced, and the native feature-gated path (gliner2/ort/tokenizers) previously only ever compiled on Linux, so a Windows/macOS build break could only surface after merge
sensor: GitHub CI: the `test` job (Linux, --all-features) and the `cross-platform` matrix (macos-latest, windows-latest: cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast then cargo check --workspace --all-features --all-targets)

invariant: The shell surfaces (`scripts/*.sh`, `.githooks/*`) pass shellcheck; the sensor WARN-skips without the tool locally and fails closed in CI
rationale: The hooks and helper scripts are load-bearing contributor and CI gates; the SC2059-class printf defects a manual sweep had to fix should surface automatically instead
sensor: bash scripts/check-shellcheck.sh (shellcheck sensor, in the verification and ci sets)

invariant: Every documented adapter selection surface is covered black-box through the compiled binary: the process-plugin `--detector`/`--judge`/`--policy`/`--transformer`/`--vault process` pairs (with a missing command failing at startup), `--process-timeout-ms`, the enforcement-context flags (`--recipient`/`--data-category`/`--purpose`/`--jurisdiction`), config auto-discovery (working directory, then `$HOME`), the explicit `--vault json` round-trip, and the `--vault-ttl-seconds` vault restriction
rationale: The library-level protocol tests prove the plugin, not the adapter: a refactor that dropped a flag-to-wiring path would keep CI green while the shipped binary silently used a built-in plugin or the default context
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield (tests/cli_process_plugins.rs, tests/cli_context.rs, tests/cli_config.rs, tests/cli_errors.rs, tests/cli_sanitize.rs)

invariant: The pipeline validates the policy plan before transforming: exactly one decision per detected entity, on the same kind and span, and a secret-kind entity is `Redact` (or `Block`/`Review`, which fail the call)
rationale: A plan that drops an entity leaves its raw value in the sanitized output, and a reversible action on a credential stores it in the vault instead of redacting it, so both defeat the boundary no matter how correct the policy was for the entities it did decide
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-core (tests::policy::short_plan_fails_closed, tests::policy::substituted_decision_fails_closed, tests::policy::reversible_action_on_secret_fails_closed)

invariant: Non-reversible transformers (`generalize`, `mask`) never emit vault-resolvable tokens or mappings: generalize replaces a pseudonymization target with a kind-only `__DO_PRIVATE_<KIND>__` token whose kind passes the placeholder grammar, mask keeps only the last four characters, and `restore` is a no-op on either output
rationale: Claiming non-reversibility while emitting a mintable token or a mapping would keep the raw value recoverable from the vault; equal values of one kind collapsing to one token is the documented trade-off, and it must not silently degrade into pseudonymization
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-transformer-generalize -p do-context-shield-transformer-mask + cargo test -p do-context-shield (tests/cli_transformers.rs)

invariant: The JSON vault encrypts at rest when a key file is configured (XChaCha20-Poly1305 envelope, fresh nonce per write, format marker as associated data): a plaintext file requires an explicit `encrypt-vault` migration, and a wrong key, a modified envelope, or a file in the other format fails closed instead of being misread
rationale: The vault file holds raw originals by design; without a key they are readable by anything that reaches the file (backups, shared machines, an accidental copy), and a silent reinterpretation of the wrong format could persist plaintext the operator believes is encrypted
sensor: cargo test -p do-context-shield-vault-json + cargo test -p do-context-shield (tests/cli_vault_encryption.rs)
